doc.title: John Heard interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995

title: Sneaking Basie's sandwiches and the ping pong bets
summary: Heard tells of stealing Basie's sandwiches on the road, the band's routine, calling him Papa, and Basie betting against his ping pong wins; the music reflected that life.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: No I guess it wasn’t. I guess it wasn’t. I was kind of like an outlaw when I joined the band I guess. Because Basie would be on the road like traveling from, we’d do a gig and it would be one of those hit and run gigs, you know? You’d get those once in a while. You’d go on the way to something you’d have to drop off, play a gig and keep going. So we had this hit and run gig down in Florida. We played in Lakeland and we had to go to Fort Lauderdale or something. So Basie always had these sandwiches in store. So I’d wait until we’d go to sleep, and I’d sneak up and rip off a sandwich. It was a routine. That’s the routine we had. Everybody used to crack up. So I’d be back there eating like crazy. And before I’d get it down, every time, I’d hear this noise up front [growl/grumble] and everybody’d say, “No Chief! No Chief! Don’t do that to him.” It was a routine every night. Every time we walked into a restaurant, we’d pull into a restaurant or something, he would have his plate there, and every time I walked by he’d start raking things in ‘cause he thought I was going to — ‘til I walked by. It’s great. I used to call him Papa. He would bet against me, on the ping pong thing, you know the ping pong thing — I was the ping pong champion. So he would bet money that someone was going to beat me. He didn’t like me winning all the time.
But all this fun stuff kind of found its way into the music, didn’t it?
That’s what the music was about. It was about the life we were living.
